advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove 'step / timeout' from the CHANGE_SETTINGS triggers in docs/config.md:567 and the matching RESOLUTION_MESSAGES text in failure.py:351-354, keeping only the token/output-length bound that actually maps to CHANGE_SETTINGS
evidence: docs/config.md:567 (changed): "A setting was rejected (credentials, model id, or a token / step / timeout bound; 401/403, non-context-length 400) — check the configured model, credentials and bounds, then retry."
src/rebar/llm/failure.py:351-354 (changed): "...or a request parameter such as a token/step/timeout bound..."
src/rebar/llm/failure.py:287-288: `if isinstance(exc, httpx.TimeoutException): return ResolutionClass.WAIT_AND_RETRY`; failure.py:292-295 does the same for botocore timeouts
docs/config.md:575-576 (unchanged, same section): "an exhausted-retry timeout still classifies `WAIT_AND_RETRY`", which contradicts the row
advisory.finding: The rewritten CHANGE_SETTINGS row in docs/config.md still lists 'step / timeout' bounds as triggers for this class. The classifier never puts either one in CHANGE_SETTINGS. Step/budget exhaustion (UsageLimitExceeded, LLMBudgetExhaustedError, RunawayToolLoopError) goes to FIX_AGENT_DESIGN, and timeouts go to WAIT_AND_RETRY. The new RESOLUTION_MESSAGES text (failure.py:351-354) repeats the same 'token/step/timeout bound' wording. The change was meant to make this text match what the class actually contains.
scenarios: An operator whose review hit the step limit or a timeout reads the taxonomy table and goes looking for a bounds setting in CHANGE_SETTINGS. The actual disposition is FIX_AGENT_DESIGN or WAIT_AND_RETRY.
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/config.md:567, change the row's trigger list to e.g. '(credentials, model id, or a token / output-length bound; 401/403, non-context-length 400, max_tokens truncation)'. Make the same change to the CHANGE_SETTINGS string in src/rebar/llm/failure.py:351-354 by replacing 'token/step/timeout bound' with 'token bound'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a presence anchor (e.g. `assert "PLAN REVIEW: INDETERMINATE for t1" in out`) before the absence asserts in the clean-run test
evidence: tests/unit/test_llm_commands_render.py:119-120: assert "model did not run" not in out / assert "build drift" not in out

No presence assertion (e.g. on the 'PLAN REVIEW:' header written at src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:483) anchors the capture in this test, unlike the sibling test at line 112 which asserts a presence.
advisory.finding: test_render_plan_review_text_clean_run_prints_no_failure_lines only checks that text is absent from the captured stdout. It never checks that the renderer actually wrote its report to the capture. If the report were redirected (for example to stderr) or the captured buffer came back empty, the test would still pass.
scenarios: A later refactor sends the plan-review text to a different stream. The clean-run test keeps passing because the captured text is empty.
advisory.suggested_fix: Inside the loop, add `assert "PLAN REVIEW: INDETERMINATE for t1" in out` before the two `not in` assertions.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with an llm_error of 400 characters asserting the rendered line contains exactly the first 300 characters and not the rest
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:439: sys.stdout.write(f"  model did not run: {str(coverage['llm_error'])[:300]}\n")
tests/unit/test_llm_commands_render.py:99 and :110 use llm_error values well under 300 characters; no test passes a long error.
advisory.finding: The new renderer cuts llm_error to 300 characters (`str(coverage['llm_error'])[:300]`), but no test passes an error longer than 300 characters. The cap could be removed or changed without any test failing.
scenarios: A provider sends back a multi-kilobyte error body. If the cap regressed, the whole body would be dumped into the text report and no test would catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test with `llm_error="x" * 300 + "TAIL"` asserting `"x" * 300 in out` and `"TAIL" not in out`.
